answer: In a star-connected 3-phase system, the windings are connected such that one end of each phase winding is joined to a common point called the neutral point ($N$), and the other three ends are connected to the supply lines ($R, Y, B$). \\ \\ **1. Relation between Line and Phase Voltages:** \\ Let $V_{ph}$ be the phase voltage across each phase winding and $V_{L}$ be the line voltage between any two lines. \\ From the phasor diagram of a balanced star connection: \\ The line voltage is the phasor difference of two phase voltages. \\ $$V_L = \sqrt{V_{ph}^2 + V_{ph}^2 + 2V_{ph}V_{ph}\cos(60^{\circ})}$$ \\ $$V_L = \sqrt{3} V_{ph}$$ \\ Also, the line current $I_L$ is equal to the phase current $I_{ph}$ ($I_L = I_{ph}$). \\ \\ **2. Formula for Three-Phase Power:** \\ Total Active Power ($P$) = $3 \times \text{Power per phase}$ \\ $$P = 3 \times (V_{ph} I_{ph} \cos\phi)$$ \\ Substituting $V_{ph} = \frac{V_L}{\sqrt{3}}$ and $I_{ph} = I_L$: \\ $$P = 3 \times \left(\frac{V_L}{\sqrt{3}}\right) \times I_L \times \cos\phi = \sqrt{3} V_L I_L \cos\phi$$
proTip: In a star connection, remember: Line current equals phase current ($I_L = I_{ph}$), but line voltage is $\sqrt{3}$ times phase voltage ($V_L = \sqrt{3} V_{ph}$).
